context: Request: all closed M&A deals whose executed agreements include indemnification sections (for an indemnification clause bank). Rubric: 15 matters with their executed agreements (1001-00003, 1001-00007, 1003-00003, 1005-00006, 1006-00007, 1008-00008, 1009-00003, 1013-00006, 1015-00004 contribution-agreement-execution.docx, 1017-00006 mipa-execution-version.docx, 1037-00006, 1039-00004 offer-to-purchase-agreement-execution.docx, 1041-00003, 1042-00004, 1046-00001 business-combination-agreement-execution.docx), plus a precision criterion.

stages.stage: List files in the document store
stages.note: Whole-store glob; reviewer said partly (capped listing, visible matters unopened).

stages.stage: List matter folders
stages.note: declared: List files in the document store (attempt 2); lists all 266 matter folder names.

stages.stage: Search file names for request keywords
stages.note: Split from the same declared span: per-matter listing of file names matching deal, agreement, closing and indemnity words (about 93K characters). Reviewer said yes but flagged generic words and a likely truncated output.

stages.stage: Scan document text with an extraction script
stages.note: Store-wide extraction script counts indemnity mentions, then a second script keeps only files whose names match acquisition-agreement types and marks which have an indemnity article. Reviewer said partly; flagged that the file-name filter could drop agreements named differently.

stages.stage: Screen candidate matters by reading documents
stages.note: declared: Read a chosen matter's documents in depth; reads the first 110-180 lines of twenty executed agreements from twenty candidate matters and lists closing file names for them.

stages.stage: Search within a candidate matter's files
stages.note: Snippet script pulls indemnity headings from the 22 chosen agreements, plus reads of closing certificates for ten of those matters (labelled by the dominant intent). Reviewer said partly; flagged that the set was fixed at 22 and closing evidence was read only for some.

stages.stage: Screen candidate matters by reading documents
stages.note: declared: List files in candidate matters; reads an agreement, certificate and two memos from two candidates with unusual file names, and judges one of them a misfiled copy of another matter. Reviewer said partly; flagged that exclusion as resting on two memos.

stages.stage: Write the response
stages.note: Writes 23 deals with clause locations, closing evidence and exclusions. Reviewer said partly; flagged a possible double-count between two matters, unopened matters, and execution-version documents counted as executed.

stages.stage: Check or revise the response
stages.note: Edits the count, deletes one matter's row as a duplicate of another deal, adds a misfile note, re-reads and sets the count to 21. Reviewer said partly; flagged that the duplicate was dropped without opening the other matter.

stages.stage: Check or revise the response
stages.note: Attempt 2. Row-count script fails on the file location, reruns on the output file (21 rows), adds a scope caveat.

stages.stage: Check or revise the response
stages.note: Attempt 3. A read made with no stage open is rejected; reopens the stage and reads the first 12 lines of the response.

stages.stage: Finish the run
stages.note: Calls finish.

runs.sequence: List files in the document store → List matter folders → Search file names for request keywords → Scan document text with an extraction script → Screen candidate matters by reading documents → Search within a candidate matter's files → Screen candidate matters by reading documents → Write the response → Check or revise the response → Finish the run
runs.failure_point: A file-name filter on agreement types dropped a matter whose agreement had another name; it then excluded one opened matter as misfiled, deleted another as a duplicate, and kept several matters that do not qualify.

first_error.stage: Scan document text with an extraction script
first_error.why: Its file-name listing had reached every needed matter, but the follow-up scan kept only files named as acquisition-agreement types, so a matter whose executed agreement has another name never entered the candidate set.
first_error.critic_note: Review [23] named the file-name filter risk; the agent later checked two candidates with unusual file names ([69]-[77]) but never re-ran the scan without the filter.

other_errors.why: It read a memo and closing memo of the needed matter at [69]-[77], judged the folder a misfiled copy of another matter because the memos carried another number, and left it out of the answer.
other_errors.critic_note: Review [77] flagged that the exclusion rested on two memos without checking the matter's own agreement; the agent went straight to writing.

other_errors.why: The answer lists several matters as closed qualifying deals that do not qualify, judged from opening lines of execution-version agreements and file names (evidence seen at [24]-[68]).
other_errors.critic_note: Reviews [68] and [83] flagged closing evidence read only for some matters and execution-version documents counted as executed; the revisions only changed counts and added a caveat.

other_errors.why: An edit deleted a needed matter's row as a duplicate of another deal although its own executed agreement had been listed, so the final answer omits it.
other_errors.critic_note: Review [83] prompted the de-duplication; review [97] then flagged that the duplicate was dropped without opening the other matter, and the agent did not revisit it.

stages.note: Reads agreements, status memos and trackers of the remaining doubtful candidates and greps two matters' documents for closing words. Reviewer said partly; flagged two matters excluded on a keyword grep with no closing document opened.

runs.failure_point: Two needed matters surfaced in its scan but were left out of the agreements it read; a third was excluded on a keyword grep; several non-qualifying deals were included.

first_error.why: The folder-restricted scan just before listed both matters, but the 24 agreements it chose to read left them out, and no later stage opened them.
first_error.critic_note: Review [61] flagged that only a subset of surfaced candidates was opened; the agent listed ten more matters it had named but not these two.

other_errors.why: It had read the needed matter's executed agreement at [29] but excluded it after a keyword grep for closing words at [89]-[90], with no closing document opened.
other_errors.critic_note: Review [92] named this exclusion and recommended opening the matter's closing documents; the agent wrote the response next.

other_errors.critic_note: Reviews [61] and [92] flagged closing status taken from file names and snippets and indemnity sections never confirmed for included matters; the agent did not re-check them.

runs.sequence: List files in the document store → Search file names for request keywords → Scan document text with an extraction script → Screen candidate matters by reading documents → Write the response → Check or revise the response → Finish the run
runs.failure_point: Its aggregated scan kept only files with deal-agreement words in the path, dropping one matter whose agreement had another name; the answer also kept several non-qualifying deals.

first_error.stage: Scan document text with an extraction script
first_error.why: The first scan had reached every needed matter, but the aggregated rerun kept only files whose paths matched deal-agreement words, so a matter whose executed agreement has another name dropped out of the candidate set.
first_error.critic_note: Review [26] flagged docx-only coverage, silent exceptions and unopened matters, not the path filter.

other_errors.why: The answer lists several matters as closed qualifying deals that do not qualify, judged from cover pages, keyword hits and short certificate reads (evidence seen at [27]-[109]).
other_errors.critic_note: Review [62] flagged included matters verified only by keyword hits and weak closing evidence for one of them; the agent reopened screening three times but read only cover pages and kept them.

divergence: All three runs failed the same criterion set in part: one needed matter whose executed agreement has a non-standard name never entered the candidate set (T0 and T2 through a file-name or path filter on agreement types after a broad scan reached it, T1 by leaving it, and another surfaced matter, out of the agreements it chose to read). All three also included non-qualifying deals judged from opening lines and file names. T0 and T1 additionally dropped opened matters on thin evidence (misfile note, duplicate removal, keyword grep), each named by a review the agent did not act on; T2 kept those matters and had the highest score.
